vulnerabilities.description: Local unprivileged users can terminate arbitrary local processes via a systemd-oomd IPC API due to a missing path traversal validation.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for the stock Liquibase Secure container, which does not run systemd-oomd.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires a running systemd-oomd service and its IPC API; the stock container starts only the Liquibase CLI and does not run systemd-oomd.

analysis.detail: This issue is in systemd-oomd's IPC API. The Liquibase Secure image inherits Ubuntu packages from the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and creates a static liquibase user with useradd rather than running systemd-managed services (`docker/Dockerfile:5`). The container entrypoint only execs a requested command or the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no references to oomd or systemd-oomd, so the required systemd-oomd IPC service is absent from the stock container environment.

vulnerabilities.description: systemd-homed contains a local privilege escalation bug via arbitrary system group addition to a local, logged in, homed-managed user.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for the stock Liquibase Secure container, which does not use systemd-homed to manage users.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires a logged-in, homed-managed user under systemd-homed; the stock container provisions a static user and does not run systemd-homed.

analysis.detail: This privilege-escalation flaw requires systemd-homed to manage a local, logged-in user. The Liquibase Secure image creates its liquibase user statically with useradd during image build (`docker/Dockerfile:5`) and the entrypoint only execs the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no homed or systemd-homed references, so the required systemd-homed runtime environment is absent.

vulnerabilities.description: In systemd 259, systemd-journald can send ANSI escape sequences to the terminals of arbitrary users when a "logger -p emerg" command is executed, if ForwardToWall=yes is set.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure's container never runs systemd-journald or any systemd service; libsystemd0 is present only as an inherited base-image library dependency.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires a running systemd-journald service with ForwardToWall enabled; Liquibase Secure's container has no init system and never runs systemd-journald or any other systemd service.

analysis.detail: This flaw requires systemd-journald to be running as a system service with ForwardToWall=yes, receiving a "logger -p emerg" invocation. A review of the running container found no systemd or systemd-journald process at all: the container has no init system, PID 1 is the Liquibase entrypoint script itself, and libsystemd0 ships only as a linked library dependency of other base-image packages, never as a running daemon. The vulnerable journald forwarding path cannot exist in a container that never runs journald.
